name: Confederate States

areaKm2.note: The 11 seceded states cover ~1.95M km2; Confederate-controlled territory in mid-1863 was smaller after Union gains in Tennessee, Louisiana and Arkansas. No historical-basemaps file has a Confederate polygon.

population.note: 1860 census, 11 seceded states: ~9.1M incl. ~3.5M enslaved (McPherson, isbn:0-19-503863-0, ch. 10). By mid-1863 Union armies held much of Tennessee, Louisiana, northern Arkansas, coastal enclaves and West Virginia, leaving ~7.5-8.5M under Confederate control.

urbanization.note: HYDE (OWID) United States 1860 = 19.8% for the whole country; the South was far less urban (~7-10%; New Orleans, the largest southern city, fell in 1862).

activePersonnel.note: Page: C.S. War Department reports 449,439 (1862) and 464,646 (1863) on the rolls; Livermore p. 47: 446,622 on Confederate returns 1 January 1863. Present for duty ran at ~55-65% of the rolls, so mid = ~300,000 present plus the navy.

trainedReserves.note: State troops, home guards and irregulars: Livermore estimates ~98,720 irregular troops not always carried on the returns.

supportPersonnel.note: Artillery ~18,000, engineers, ordnance and quartermaster ~6,000, navy and marines ~4,000. Reconstruction.

mobilizationRatio.note: Page: enlistment estimates range from ~750,000 to 1,227,890-1,406,180 over the war, from ~5.5M free inhabitants, i.e. 8-15% of the total population incl. the enslaved.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Infantry present, all departments, mid-1863. Army of Northern Virginia ~75,000 at Gettysburg, Army of Tennessee ~45,000, Vicksburg garrison ~30,000.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: imported Enfields and captured Springfields, shortages of shoes and kit

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: veteran regiments by 1863

count.note: Confederate cavalry present (Stuart, Forrest, Wheeler, Morgan).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: own horses, muzzle-loading carbines and shotguns

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: skilled riders and raiders

count.note: Educated guess: field guns; the Army of Northern Virginia had ~280 guns at Gettysburg.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: mixed calibres, unreliable fuses, captured pieces

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: battalion organisation good

count.note: Ironclad rams and cruisers in service, mid-1863 (page: at least twenty ironclads commissioned over the whole war; commerce raiders Alabama and Florida at sea).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: slow casemate ironclads with weak engines

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: ex-US Navy officers, scratch crews

count.note: Educated guess: gunboats, rams, torpedo boats (David) and river craft.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: scratch crews

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.75. Evidence: Lee and Longstreet in Virginia; weaker western command (Bragg, Pemberton)

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.5-0.75. Evidence: state regiments with strong identity; desertion rising after July 1863

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.75. Evidence: defence of the homeland after Chancellorsville, shaken by Gettysburg and Vicksburg

weapons.note: Anchor: between 6 (1805) and 7 (1905). Evidence: rifle-muskets, imported Whitworths, fewer breech-loaders

ships.note: Anchor: between 6 and 7. Evidence: improvised ironclads, first successful submarine attack (Hunley, 1864) still ahead

fortification.note: Anchor: between 6 and 7. Evidence: Charleston and Vicksburg earthworks, naval mines (torpedoes)

logistics.note: Anchor: between 6 and 7. Evidence: decaying railways, gauge breaks, Tredegar the only big iron works

communications.note: Anchor: between 6 and 7. Evidence: telegraph, signal corps

isr.note: Anchor: between 6 and 7. Evidence: cavalry scouting, Stuart absent before Gettysburg

air.note: No military aircraft before 1911; balloons, where used, are counted under ISR.

gdpPerCapita.note: Analogue: Maddison Project 2023 (OWID) United States 1863 = 4,734; southern income per head incl. the enslaved was ~80% of the national mean in 1860 (Engerman), less after blockade and war damage.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess: Confederate war spending, financed largely by paper money and inflation, absorbed roughly a quarter or more of output in 1863; low = US antebellum peacetime share.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess: the South had ~10% of US manufacturing capacity in 1860.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess: cotton economy; food shortages and Richmond bread riot (April 1863).

annualCohort.note: Analogue ratio of the France 1805 snapshot (males reaching military age ~1.05% per year) applied to the ~5.5M free population only, as the enslaved were not conscripted.

artillery.note: Educated guess: field guns per year, mostly from Tredegar (Richmond) and Selma.

ships_major.note: Educated guess: ironclads completed per year.

roadKm.note: Educated guess: few engineered roads; dirt roads impassable in rain.

railKm.note: About 9,000 miles (14,500 km) in the 11 states in 1861 (McPherson ch. 10; CHAT US total 1861 = 49,412 km, https://data.nber.org/chat/chat.dta); lines lost in Tennessee, Louisiana and Virginia by mid-1863.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess: Charleston, Wilmington, Mobile, Savannah, Galveston (blockaded).

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess: blockade runners and coastal craft.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess: thin wagon and rail supply.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess: horses and mules under Confederate control; heavy losses by 1863.

homeDefense.note: 1.2 row: familiar terrain, fortified ports and cities, white population support.

notes: Snapshot = Confederate States in July 1863. Territory and population = the area under Confederate control (1860 census base of the 11 seceded states, less Union-held areas); includes is empty. Border: no historical-basemaps polygon exists for the Confederacy at any year, so border is none. Personnel: troops present and navy = active; state troops, home guards and irregulars = trainedReserves. Of the ~8M inhabitants ~3.5M were enslaved and not armed; mobilizable is computed on the total population, so the ratio is set against the total. Strengths from the Confederate States Army page (War Department reports), Livermore (1900) and McPherson; branch split is a reconstruction (grade C/D).
